title: Logging and Application Observability
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of logging and application observability using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates logging and application observability.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Logging and Application Observability** as part of **Serialization, Networking, and Application Integration**. Integration code must validate external data, handle timeouts and failure states, keep credentials outside source control, and test boundary behavior. Use the subtopics—Structured Logging, Correlation IDs and Context, Metrics, Traces, and Diagnostics—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.
